title: SDK edge recovery & telemetry mini-quickstart (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, deployable mini-quickstart for SDK integrators that bundles: a minimal onboarding flow, an agreed telemetry event contract (sample events + property names), and 3 pragmatic edge-recovery patterns (retry/circuit/fallback). The goal is a single-page handoff engineers can follow during a 15–30 minute demo or first integration spike.

Audience:
- Integrator engineers (mobile/web/backend) doing a first Redwood SDK integration
- SREs and oncall owners validating observability and failure modes
- Solutions engineers doing customer handoffs

Scope (what this doc contains):
- Minimal code snippets to wire SDK + telemetry (Python + Node samples)
- Concrete telemetry event names and property keys (keep small)
- 3 edge-recovery patterns with config examples and tradeoffs
- Lightweight alerting / dashboard suggestions and handoff checklist

Out of scope:
- Full ingestion pipeline or schema enforcement (see Confluence linked_artifacts)
- Long-form SDK API reference

Prerequisites:
- Redwood SDK installed (pip install redwood-sdk or npm i @redwood/sdk)
- API key available and scoped for sandbox projects
- Instrumentation destination configured (otel/rdw-exporter or built-in telemetry)

Quickstart (15 minutes):
1) Bootstrap the client (2 min)
Python (pseudo):

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED", telemetry_enabled=True)

Node (pseudo):
const { RedwoodClient } = require('@redwood/sdk')
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, telemetryEnabled: true })

2) Add a small wrapper to capture events and enrich with runtime metadata (2–4 min)
- Enrich events with: sdk_version, environment (dev/stage/prod), region, request_id.
- Attach a lightweight latency histogram for each request.

3) Exercise a sample generation and emit standard events (3 min)
- Call the API with a short prompt and emit events described below. Ensure errors emit the error contract.

4) Verify events in the telemetry sink / dashboard (3–6 min)
- Check presence of request.start, request.success, request.error, and fallback.invoked. Validate property keys.

Minimal telemetry contract (keep small — these will be used in alerts and dashboards):
- request.start
  - properties: request_id, sdk_version, environment, region, model_name, model_revision, input_tokens
- request.success
  - properties: request_id, duration_ms, output_tokens, cost_estimate_cents
- request.error
  - properties: request_id, error_code (string), error_message (short), duration_ms, retryable (bool)
- fallback.invoked
  - properties: request_id, primary_model, fallback_model, reason, latency_primary_ms
- cache.hit / cache.miss
  - properties: request_id, cache_key, ttl_seconds

Example event (as emitted text for the sink):
request.error {"request_id":"r-123","error_code":"model_oom","error_message":"out of memory","duration_ms":2400,"retryable":false}

Edge-recovery patterns (practical, minimal configs):
1) Retry-with-conservative-backoff (recommended default)
- When: for transient network errors or rate-limit responses (5xx/429)
- Config: max_retries=2, initial_backoff=100ms, multiplier=3, jitter=true
- Tradeoffs: small latency amplification on transient failures; reduces SRE pages for transient flakiness.
- Telemetry: emit request.retry with attempt number and last_error.

2) Circuit breaker to protect GPU pools (recommended for high-throughput clients)
- When: repeated 5xx or sustained latency spikes for a model/route
- Config: failure_threshold=10 over 60s, cooldown=30s, probe_interval=10s
- Behavior: short-circuit requests to a local error response and emit fallback.invoked if fallback available
- Telemetry: emit circuit.open / circuit.closed with scope=model_name and current_failure_count

3) Graceful fallback to cheaper/quantized variants (recommended for cost-tolerant flows)
- When: when latency SLOs are breached or primary model OOMs/fails
- Config: fallback_chain = ["gpt-small-q4", "gpt-medium-q4"] ; fallback_policy = on_error | on_latency_threshold
- Tradeoffs: quality may degrade; ensure prompt conditioning adapts to smaller model context windows
- Telemetry: emit fallback.invoked with reason and relative_quality_hint (optional)

Sample config snippet (YAML-like text for integration teams):
recovery:
  retries:
    max_retries: 2
    backoff_ms: 100
  circuit_breakers:
    - model: big-gpu-model
      failures: 10
      window_seconds: 60
      cooldown_seconds: 30
  fallbacks:
    - trigger: on_latency_threshold
      threshold_ms: 700
      chain: ["small-q4", "medium-q4"]

Alerting & dashboard suggestions (minimal):
- Dashboard: Requests per minute, 95p latency, error rate by error_code, fallback rate, retry rate
- Alerts (examples):
  - High error rate: error_rate > 3% for 5m -> page SRE
  - Latency regression: p95 latency > 700ms for 10m -> notify product and eng oncall
  - Fallback surge: fallback_rate > 1% sustained for 15m -> pager to services-eng

Handoff checklist (to include with customer / team handoff):
- [ ] Confirm API key + environment mapping (dev/stage/prod)
- [ ] Confirm telemetry sink is receiving request.start / request.success / request.error
- [ ] Install local dashboards: p95 latency, rpm, error_rate, fallback_rate
- [ ] Decide fallback chain for key routes and add to config store
- [ ] Agree SLOs: latency p50/p95, error budget (e.g. 0.1% fatal errors)
- [ ] Run synthetic tests that simulate 429/5xx/oom and validate recovery flows

Operational notes & gotchas:
- Do not treat retryable=true on model_oom — prefer fallback rather than retrying into same model.
- Prefer emitting structured error_code values (snake_case) not free-form messages.
- Keep telemetry property set narrow to avoid cardinality explosion (avoid user_id in every event unless necessary).
- Ensure sampling for high-volume endpoints to manage ingestion cost; include sampling_rate property when sampling applied.

Open questions for follow-up:
- Should fallback.invoked include a small quality metric (BLEU-like) or instead rely on eval harnesses?
- Standardized mapping of error_code taxonomy across client libs (we should add to SDK spec).

Next steps / proposed owners:
- Miguel: add Node + Swift sample snippets to the repo (PR template ready)
- Samir: prototype circuit-breaker lib wrapper for SDK (Spike 2 days)
- Aisha (owner): finalize the telemetry contract and update Confluence; coordinate with observability to add dashboards

Notes to integrators (short):
- Start small: wire request.start and request.success first, then add request.error and fallback.invoked.
- Run 10–20 synthetic requests and inspect the events before doing broader load tests.
- Use the recovery presets above as a baseline; tune thresholds per workload.

If you want, I can convert this sketch into a single-page README with copy-ready code blocks for Python/Node and a matching short Postman collection for the first exercise.
